subject: Cognitive Science
title: Sleep and Memory Consolidation
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Sleep and Memory Consolidation.

hook.text: Your brain doesn't rest during sleep. It replays the day's learning over and over, strengthening memories.

buildup.text: Sleep spindles—bursts of neural activity during Stage 2 sleep—transfer memories to long-term storage.

discovery.text: REM sleep consolidates procedural and emotional memories. Slow-wave sleep handles facts and events.

twist.text: Losing just two hours of sleep cuts memory consolidation dramatically—even if you feel fine.

climax.text: A nap after studying beats caffeine. Your sleeping brain literally rehearses what you just learned.

punchline.text: Sleep is studying with your eyes closed.

quiz.question: What role do sleep spindles play in memory?
options: They help transfer memories to long-term storage
They only occur during REM sleep
